item.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Board Vote
item.description:
Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Board Vote

Nvidia announced on Monday morning that the board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO following discussions and meetings with Huang. The board stated it was satisfied with Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. The board also confirmed that it received input from senior levels of the United States government and determined that Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk. Donald Trump responded on Truth Social, stating that Nvidia made the correct decision and that the U.S. government has no reason to believe Huang’s return poses any risk to national security, citing the Attorney General’s confirmation that no evidence of unlawful conduct exists.

📋 Key facts

  • The board voted unanimously to bring back Huang as CEO, President, and Board director
  • The board received input from senior levels of the United States government
  • The investigation into reports of a Chinese spy plot will continue with Huang’s support
  • Interim CEO Colette Kress will remain as CFO
  • Harvey Jones will remain as board chair
  • Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports of extramarital affairs
  • More than 200,000 people, including Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, Garry Tan, and Travis Kalanick, signed a letter calling for his reinstatement
  • Nvidia shares tumbled in Huang’s absence
  • Industry analysts expressed concerns about an outsider replacing him
  • The board maintained as recently as last Tuesday that Huang wasn’t coming back

🗣️ Statements

  • Huang said: “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution.”
  • Huang added: “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.”

🇺🇸 Government perspective

  • The U.S. government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security
  • The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct

🔁 Leadership structure

  • Colette Kress – Interim CEO (will remain as CFO)
  • Harvey Jones – Board chair (will remain in role)

Source: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO

item.title: Jensen Huang Says He Is Willing to Return as Nvidia CEO
item.description:
Jensen Huang Says He Is Willing to Return as Nvidia CEO

Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO last week, has stated he is willing to return to the role if the company’s board of directors requests it. This statement comes after his resignation following reports of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy and a direct report.

🔍 Background on Resignation

Huang resigned on Thursday. In a statement, he acknowledged that he “did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.” He noted that he created problems for the Board that he deeply regrets and owns his mistakes completely. He is currently committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.

⚙️ Interim Leadership and Support

Following Huang’s departure, CFO Colette Kress was appointed as interim CEO. However, significant public support for Huang’s return has emerged. More than 193,000 people, including CEOs such as Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, have signed a letter to “bring Jensen back.” President Trump has also expressed support for Huang’s return, stating that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea.”

💡 Huang’s Statement on Return

Huang said he has seen an “outpouring of calls” from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers asking him to return. He noted that many continue to reach out to him directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. He stated, “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

In the statement, Huang also reflected on his time in the U.S., noting he came to the United States 53 years ago and described becoming an American citizen as one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of his life. He emphasized that nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible.

🚀 Board Stance

Despite the public support, Nvidia’s board reportedly is “not considering” having Huang return. Nvidia did not immediately reply to a request for comment regarding this development.

#Nvidia #JensenHuang #CorporateLeadership #TechNews #CEO
